items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Wade must have gotten wind of something... I never saw or heard anything of the Wades again.

ctx.x: He must have given our address as the one where he lived because some detectives came there and questioned me. Wade must have gotten wind of something because the whole family had gone out and left me alone there. The detectives told me that Charlie had been burglarizing stores in the up-town shopping district. They had come with a search warrant to look for some/the stolen goods, but nothing was there. The door of the small room where Wade had his malt working, was locked. I had never seen what was in that room…

whiskey. The detectives took all the soap powder they could find, any old dirty rags and garbage and put them in those barrels of malt or mash to make certain that it could not be used anymore. I never saw or heard anything of the Wades again.

I stayed in the apartment alone for a few days and at with the Hustons. Then Mrs. Huston's son said he was going back to the South where he could carry a gun and I lived with Mrs. Huston, giving her a certain amount every week for my room and board.
